speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources in light of the permanent closure of the Sungei Road flea market (a) how many of the vendors have been offered assistance and what kind of assistance has been rendered; and (b) how many vendors are not receiving these assistance and why are they not receiving them.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Further engagements between the SSOs and some of the remaining permit holders are ongoing.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, there is no such dialogue at this moment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the first question, Mdm Speaker, NEA will be the lead agency to coordinate with the other agencies, the Mayors, and also ask other Advisers who may be the Advisers in the constituencies where these hawkers live, so that if they approach them, they will know where to refer them to.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For this, the lead agency will be NEA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the second question, I think we have to note that SRHZ does have a long history, from the 1930s.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And for some Singaporeans, they hold strong memories.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But, again, we must recognise there were really many places that have moved on and where street hawking was quite popular and even a common sight in the past.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the years, in the 1970s and 1980s, many of them have moved on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They are now housed in our hawker centres as well as markets and I believe many of them have also done well.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Despite all these, we have retained SRHZ so that the original 31 rag-and-bone permit holders can continue their trade.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But over the years, we have seen a fair number of others who have come to SRHZ.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, after so many years, only 11 are still operating there.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Now, despite all the disamenities and even the residents accommodating the hawkers for these many, many years, for example, the obstruction of public roads, storage of goods in public places, sometimes people sleeping around in the residential estates, we have continued to accommodate these until such time when the place would be required for development.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am surprised that the Association for the Recycling of Second Hand Goods is surprised that we are moving on because we have been engaging everybody since 2012.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have already told them that when the time comes, notice would be given and we have to move on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, the time has come and we have engaged enough and I think to meet them again is to almost promise that we will change our stance and that redevelopment would not start.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think the Association understood that the SRHZ would be removed.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: What the Minister has spoken seems to show that such micro economy is actually a livelihood for some other people who have since joined.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, I think they are really looking for an alternative site which can be managed in such a way that all the disamenities that the Minister was talking about can be mitigated.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I would urge the Ministry to consider engaging with them so that we can look at such possibilities, especially since such outdoor markets, as the Minister said, we have been losing them and this is probably the last one.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Having one would actually be good for our cultural landscape.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I empathise with the pleading of our Member.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think we may stand to lose something which is very important or memorable for some of us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But then, again, we also have to balance this with the needs of our country and to be fair to the many, many other hawkers who have moved on, gone to markets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And for those who need to peddle their wares occasionally, they have also been able to do well in trade fairs where they pay for the rents and are well-managed so that the disamenities mentioned do not exist.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, if the question is: are there alternatives?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But should we put up another site like this which is deemed to be like Sungei Road but not at Sungei Road, I do not think this is something we want to dwell on further.
